Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

The test `['org.apache.commons.codec.binary.StringUtilsTest.testEqualsCS1()']` failed.
The test looks like:

```java
223 :     @Test
224 :     public void testEqualsCS1() {
225 :         Assert.assertFalse(StringUtils.equals(new StringBuilder("abc"), null));
226 :         Assert.assertFalse(StringUtils.equals(null, new StringBuilder("abc")));
227 :         Assert.assertTrue(StringUtils.equals(new StringBuilder("abc"), new StringBuilder("abc")));
228 :         Assert.assertFalse(StringUtils.equals(new StringBuilder("abc"), new StringBuilder("abcd"))); // error occurred here
231 :     }
```

It failed with the following error message and call stack:

```
java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: String index out of range: 3
	at java.lang.AbstractStringBuilder.charAt(AbstractStringBuilder.java:237)
	at java.lang.StringBuilder.charAt(StringBuilder.java:76)
	at org.apache.commons.codec.binary.CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches(CharSequenceUtils.java:59)
	at org.apache.commons.codec.binary.StringUtils.equals(StringUtils.java:81)
	at org.apache.commons.codec.binary.StringUtilsTest.testEqualsCS1(StringUtilsTest.java:228)
```

The failing test `org.apache.commons.codec.binary.StringUtilsTest.testEqualsCS1()` covers classes `CharSequenceUtils` and `StringUtils`. Next, let's retrieve the failing methods covered by the `StringUtils` class.

The failing test covering the `StringUtils` class is the method `equals(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.CharSequence)`. The failed test endpoint at line 228 in the`StringUtilsTest` is calling the `StringUtils.equals` method with two `StringBuilder` instances. The error occurred at line 228 when trying to compare two `StringBuilder` instances with different lengths, resulting in a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`. This happens because the `equals` method implementation is expecting `CharSequence` instances instead of `StringBuilder` instances, leading to an incorrect comparison logic.

It seems there is a mismatch in the parameter types passed to the `equals` method. The `equals` method should be modified to accept `CharSequence` instances instead of `StringBuilder` instances to prevent this error from occurring. Below are the methods that need to be fixed:

```
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.StringUtils.equals(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.CharSequence)
```
